title: Plug-and-Play SDK telemetry checklist and quickstart notes
summary: Working notes describing a minimal plug-and-play SDK quickstart that ships with a lightweight telemetry checklist. Targeted at SDK maintainers and integrators who want to onboard with minimal configuration and safe observability defaults.
body:
Purpose:
Small, shareable doc for SDK teams to include with starter kits. The goal is a 5-10 minute integration that emits reliable telemetry (events, traces, cost tokens) without a heavy onboarding burden. This is intentionally prescriptive — opinionated defaults + escape hatches.

Audience:
- Integrators (product/platform engineers) embedding Redwood SDKs into sample apps or demos.
- SDK maintainers who own telemetry contracts.
- Solutions engineers who do short POC sessions.

Constraints and principles (design notes):
1) Default to minimal, low-cardinality telemetry: a small set of events and a single trace id per request.
2) Preserve privacy: never collect prompt/response text in production default. Provide an opt-in debug mode.
3) Fail-open: SDK telemetry must not block requests or add visible latency > 20ms median.
4) Cost-awareness: emit token counters and model id, but avoid token-by-token streams in telemetry payloads.
5) Local-first: provide a local stub mode so early experiments do not hit production endpoints.

Quickstart (5-min path) - high level steps (copy into quickstart readme):
- 1) Install: `yarn add @redwood/sdk` or `pip install redwood-sdk`
- 2) Init: `redwood init --minimal-telemetry` (creates .redwood/telemetry.toml)
- 3) Wire: import SDK, call `client.generate()` in example route.
- 4) Verify: run `redwood telemetry inspect` to see events emitted to local dev collector.
- 5) Enable debug (optional): set `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=debug` to capture prompt/response locally only.

Telemetry checklist (opinionated items for the SDK to implement by default):
- Core events (low-cardinality): `request_started`, `request_finished`, `request_failed`, `model_switch`
- Request attributes: `sdk_version`, `client_lang`, `model_id`, `sequence_length_estimate`
- Cost metrics: `input_tokens_estimate`, `output_tokens_estimate`, `billing_model`
- Latency: `server_latency_ms` (server-side), `client_side_end_to_end_ms` (measured in SDK)
- Trace id: `trace_id` attached to all events for a request; compatible with vendor tracing systems (OTel/traceparent header).
- Sampling: default 1% event sampling for verbose traces, 100% sampling for core events. Provide `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING` override.
- Error annotation: include `error_code` (internal mapping), `http_status`, short `error_message` (sanitized, < 256 chars).
- Privacy modes: `off` (no prompt text), `local_debug` (prompts allowed but not uploaded), `full` (enterprise feature, must be enabled via console).

Minimal telemetry wire format (for docs / contract):
- Event envelope (JSON): `{"trace_id":"<uuid>","event":"request_started","attrs":{...}}`
- Keep attributes flat, no nested objects.
- Max event payload size default: 4 KB (configurable).

Sample snippets (developer-facing, short):
- Node quick example (one-liner): `await client.generate({prompt: 'Summarize X', telemetry:{traceId: 'auto'}})`
- Python: `client.generate('Summarize X', telemetry={'mode':'local_debug'})`
- Local stub startup: `redwood stub --listen 127.0.0.1:8000` then set SDK env `REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000`

Common failure modes & mitigation notes (for SDK authors):
- Telemetry proxy outage: SDK should buffer up to N=500 events in local disk queue; drop oldest on overflow and emit a single `telemetry_dropped` event.
- High-card telemetry causing cost: enforce attribute cardinality whitelist; warn and disable by default.
- User accidentally shipping prompt capture: default to `off`, require explicit flag AND admin console toggle for enabling in production.
- Latency regressions when tracing: use async non-blocking post; use exponential backoff for retries; do not retry on 5xx more than 2 times.

Operational playbook (what solutions / SE should do during a POC):
- Pre-POC: add `telemetry.toml` to sample repo, enable `local_debug` for capture.
quickstart_steps: Install SDK -> `npm i @redwood/sdk` or `pip install redwood-sdk`
Run sample -> hit example route and confirm `request_started` shows in `redwood telemetry inspect`
Enable debug locally -> `export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=local_debug` and re-run if you need prompt traces
telemetry_checklist: Emit core events: request_started, request_finished, request_failed, model_switch
Attach trace_id and sdk_version to every event
Estimate and emit token counts (input/output) without raw text
Respect privacy defaults: prompt capture off by default
Implement retry/backoff and local disk buffering for telemetry upload
Provide sampling config with sensible default (1% verbose traces)
Expose a single env var to toggle modes for quick demos: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY
Document retention/PII handling in README and admin console mapping
failure_modes: Telemetry endpoint unreachable -> buffer to disk -> emit telemetry_dropped event once
Large cardinality attr -> detect and replace with hashed token OR drop attribute
Retry storms -> enforce client-side rate limit for telemetry sends
User enables full capture in production -> block enable behind console toggle + audit log
sample_snippets: // Node minimal: const client = new RedwoodClient(); await client.generate({prompt: 'Hello', telemetry:{traceId: 'auto'}})

# Python minimal
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
client.generate('Hello', telemetry={'mode':'local_debug'})

# Local stub
$ redwood stub --listen 127.0.0.1:8000
$ export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
# run sample app
